answer: A sports venue I visited that left a strong impression on me was the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium in Mirpur, Dhaka, which is the main home ground of the Bangladesh team. I went there a couple of years ago with my brother-in-law to watch a one-day international, and it was my first time watching live cricket at that level. Cricket is almost a religion in my country, so the atmosphere was electric long before the game even started; people were queuing outside hours in advance, with their faces painted red and green. The stadium was absolutely [[packed to the rafters]], with thousands of fans singing, blowing horns and waving flags. When our team hit a boundary or took a wicket, the roar of the crowd was genuinely [[thunderous]], and I could feel the energy in my chest. What made it so memorable was the incredible sense of [[unity]]; complete strangers were hugging and celebrating together as one. Watching a match on television simply cannot compare to being there in person. The whole experience was thrilling and completely [[immersive]]. We bought snacks from the vendors walking up and down the stands and stayed until the very last ball. Honestly, by the end I had lost my voice from cheering, but I did not care in the slightest, especially as we won comfortably. It was one of the most exciting days of my life, and I would [[jump at the chance]] to go again.

followUps.q: Do you prefer watching sports live or on TV?
followUps.answer: Live, definitely, for the atmosphere, although I watch most matches on television because tickets are hard to get and the stadium is far from Sirajganj. At home, at least, you get the replays and commentary.
Only casually now. As a boy I played every afternoon with friends in the field near our house, but these days I prefer watching, and I occasionally join a friendly match during the holidays.

note: Named the real stadium (Sher-e-Bangla, Mirpur) and dropped the 'tens of thousands' figure; added who and when, queues and face paint; 'packed' widened to 'packed to the rafters', added 'jump at the chance'.
